Class AimRule

java.lang.Object
dev.swordai.core.rl.AimRule
public final class AimRule extends Object
The camera is brought onto the opponent for the fighter in the ticks after it has been hit, for as long as it has not hit back: the ticks in which it is thrown into the air and comes down again, which is where the swing it owes is made (see AnswerRule), as a critical hit if the opponent is still in reach.

Why it is a rule. That swing is only made with the opponent under the crosshair, and after a hit it mostly was not: of the falls after a hit in which the opponent stayed within a sword's reach, half went by without the crosshair on it once. The hit moves the fighter, an opponent that goes round it has moved on, and one that hit it from the side or from behind was never in the picture. So for those ticks the turn is not left to the network: with the opponent on screen the camera goes to the middle of it, as fast as the hand (AimMotor) gets there without going past; with nothing on screen it turns, at the hand's full speed, to the side the opponent was last seen on, or, never having seen it, away from the way the hit threw the fighter, which is where the hit came from.

The same is done in the air of a jump that is made for it (JumpIn): the hit at the end of a running jump needs the crosshair on an opponent that is itself running, and one such jump in six came down with that opponent in reach and not under it. And, more gently, on an opponent that is far away (FarRest).

It goes by what the network is shown: where the opponent is on screen, and the fighter's own body.

Not thread-safe; one per fighter.

    • reset

    • level

      public void level(boolean on)
      Whether the camera is brought level with the fighter's own eye where the opponent's body spans that height, and onto the nearest part of it where it does not, instead of onto the middle of it; see Config.aimLevel. The game's reach is measured along the crosshair: from the eye down to the middle of an opponent on the same ground at the edge of the reach that ray is some 0.07 blocks longer than the level one, which is the margin by which the scripted opponents, aiming level, out-reached the fighter in the traces of 22 October.
